title: Put the lid on a gift box: seat a close-fitting lid squarely, without wedging
instruction: Put the lid on the gift box: seat it fully over the base with the gift inside, square and without wedging it. Leave the box where it is.
context: Putting the lid on a gift box, a shoebox or a jewellery box is something nearly everyone has done, and anyone watching sees at once what the robot is doing. When the lid fits closely it has to be brought down level and in line: a lid tilted or turned by a degree or two catches on the base's rim and sticks half on, and a hard push dents the walls. The job ends with the lid fully down, the box square and left where it was packed. The box is a two-piece rigid gift box that any lab can build from 2 mm greyboard to the cut list in the setup, with the play checked by feeler gauge.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up; arm bases at y +30.5 cm and -30.5 cm. Build the box from 2.0 mm greyboard (bookbinding board, sold in art-supply shops, about 10 USD a sheet), cut with a craft knife and steel rule and glued with PVA. (1) Base: open box. Cut a floor 70 x 114 mm, two long walls 114 x 38 mm standing on the floor's long edges and two short walls 66 x 38 mm between them. Outside 70 (x) x 114 (y) x 40 (z) mm (66 x 110 mm inside), about 0.05 kg, standing on the table at x 330 mm, y -70 mm. (2) Gift: a block of oak 55 x 105 x 28 mm, 0.12 kg (weigh it; trim to within 0.01 kg), lying flat in the base, long side along y, its top 30 mm over the table, 10 mm below the base's rim. (3) Lid: a top panel 79 x 123 mm, two long skirt walls 123 x 34 mm glued under the panel's long edges and two short walls 75 x 34 mm between them. 79 x 123 mm outside, 75 x 119 mm inside, 36 mm tall, about 0.05 kg. Its inside is 2.5 mm larger than the base's outside on every side. It stands top panel up, skirt down, on the table at x 330 mm, y -290 mm, its long side along y. The play is fixed by the cut list (lid inside 75 x 119 minus base outside 70 x 114 is 5 mm, so 2.5 mm a side); cutting every piece within 0.2 mm keeps it within 2.5 +/- 0.4 mm. Check each pair with calipers and a feeler gauge before use: base height 40 mm and lid height 36 mm within 0.5 mm, and 2.0 to 3.0 mm of play on all four sides with the lid held over the base; otherwise rebuild the lid. (4) Seated means the lid's top panel rests on the base's rim: the lid's top outer face 42 mm over the table (40 mm of base plus the 2 mm panel), the skirt over the base's walls by 34 mm, its rim 6 mm over the table. Bare greyboard on greyboard and on the table; the simulator uses friction 0.45 board on board and on the table and 0.5 board on gripper, and the real trial is not tuned to them. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: End state, read at the last step from the poses of the base, lid and product and both grippers. Seated: the lid's top outer face within 1.5 mm of 42 mm over the table (base 40 mm plus the 2 mm panel). Square: the lid's yaw within 1.5 degrees of the base's and its top face tilted under 1.0 degree. Centred: the lid's centre within 3.5 mm of the base's (top view). Engaged: the lid upright (tilt under 10 degrees), its centre within 8 mm of the base's and its skirt's lowest point 10 mm or more below the base's rim. On the base: the lid upright within 30 degrees, its centre within 25 mm of the base's and its lowest point 4 mm or more over the table. Box still: the base within 20 mm of where it began (top view), on the table within 3 mm and tilted under 2 degrees. Hands off: on every step of the last 1 s both grippers' finger zones are 30 mm or more from the base, lid and product, and over that 1 s each part moves under 1 mm and turns under 0.3 degrees. Score 0 if at any time the lid or base falls more than 10 mm below the table top or the product's centre leaves the base's inside, and 0 unless hands off and box still. Otherwise: 1.0 seated, square and centred; 0.5 engaged but not 1.0; 0.25 the lid on the base otherwise; 0 anything else (a lid on the table, upside down or off the base). Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. Success: 1.0 held for 1 s. Doing nothing scores 0. In a real trial: seated, calipers or a steel rule from the table to the lid's top (1.5 mm); square, a try-square on the lid's side against the base and a phone level on the lid's top (1.0 degree); centred, a feeler gauge in the gap on each side; engaged, a rule against the skirt's rim; box still, a pencil outline and a rule; hands off, a 30 mm spacer against each hand and 30 fps video; stillness is read as no visible motion of the part against a pencil outline and a taped 1 mm tick over the last 1 s (0.3 degrees is a sim check). Also in a real trial: score 0 if a wall is dented or creased more than 2 mm (a 2 mm feeler).
fidelity: Rigid bodies: the boards are 2 mm rigid plates, so nothing flexes, dents or tears (a real trial adds a dent check). Friction (0.45 board on board, 0.5 board on gripper) is a simulator setting; the real greyboard is not tuned to it and it is not scored. Box and gift sizes and masses follow the cut list and block in the setup. The paper wrap, tissue and ribbon of a real gift pack are not modelled.
reset_notes: Lay the oak block in the base, long side along y, base at x 330, y -70 mm. Stand the lid top up at x 330, y -290 mm, long side along y. Before the first trial and after any hard push, re-check the pair with calipers and a feeler gauge (play 2.0 to 3.0 mm each side). Replace a box whose walls are dented or creased more than 2 mm; keep a spare pair built from the same cut list.
